newsitem.title: PERU: Peruvians in Lima oppose Fujimori reelection -poll.
newsitem.headline: Peruvians in Lima oppose Fujimori reelection -poll.

text.p: Most Peruvians in Lima oppose a possible bid by President Alberto Fujimori for a third term in office from 2000, a new poll showed on Tuesday.
According to a survey of 498 residents of the capital by local pollster Peruana de Opinion Publica, some 52 percent opposed a Fujimori reelection bid while 37 percent were in favour.
The poll was taken last week, after Fujimori's popularity soared in the wake of a successful military raid to release hostages held by Marxist rebels for more than four months.
Fujimori's lowest approval rating since coming to power in 1990 was reversed overnight after the operation and has nearly doubled to more than 70 percent, according to other recent polls.

The Peruana de Opinion Publica poll said that 52 percent believed Fujimori had taken the decision to storm the residence on April 22 because it was the right time, while 41 percent believe he did it to increase his popularity.
The polling organisation gave no margin of error.

Congress voted last year to let Fujimori stand for a third time in 2000 if he wishes, but this has been challenged in the nation's constitutional court and opposition lawmakers are calling for a referendum on the issue.

Fujimori has dodged the issue. In a recent interview with Reuters, he said: "I prefer to combat on the job in hand over the next three years -- working for the country, combating poverty -- rather than what might happen in the year 2000."
